Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can one generic stack represent every architecture?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Declare the actual layers and process.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Fan-out, interposer, and stacked packages have different routes and process gates. Trace the visual in order: architecture; interfaces; checks. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Choose a package cross-section and identify die, bond, RDL or interposer, substrate, and cooling boundary.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Choose a package cross-section and identify die, bond, RDL or interposer, substrate, and cooling boundary. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
